title: First Lines: A Rune Primer
author: Forge-Thane Dagrund Ironvein
pages: First line, the Stand. One cut, top to bottom, true and plumb. It means: this holds. Every rune begins with the Stand, as every hold begins with a wall. If your Stand wavers, stop and go home.
Second line, the Bar. Across the Stand, at the height of your heart. It means: no further. Cut it into doors and gates. Cut it deep. A shallow Bar is a lie, and stone remembers lies.
Third line, the Root. Down and away from the Stand, like a buttress. It means: endure. Cut it on tools and blades. The Root costs more of you than the others. You will feel it in your name.
A rune is a promise in stone. The smith gives a sliver of their ancestral name to make it keep. Cut too many and you will forget your grandfather's face. That is the price. Cut what matters.
Never cut for outsiders. Never cut by guesswork. Never cut star-iron without a Forge-Thane present. And never, ever cut the Sealing on a tomb you mean to open again.
